label: D2 after a2 -> S2 (common), late in the episode (trial ~62-94)
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when S2 is the state shown (100% of activation mass at in_state==2); 99% of mass is a2 -> S2 common transitions, while a1 -> S2 rare transitions barely activate it. It also depends strongly on position in the episode: it never fires before episode trial ~50, ramps up over trials 60-89, and drops off in trials 90-99, so it looks like it carries an episode-clock signal. All variables are observed at D2 (the input itself, plus elapsed time). Inactive at D1 and GO, and on any S1 arrival. Activation mass skews toward trials whose previous outcome was rewarded (prev_reward==1 holds 87% of mass). Excluding steps that follow a rare unrewarded trial raises F1 only slightly on dev (0.83 vs 0.82), so the simpler predicate is the one recorded. Remaining false positives are a2->S2c steps in the time window where the feature stays silent, often after a rare unrewarded or unrewarded previous trial.

issues: All factual claims check out on dev. The feature has no activation at D1 or GO, all of its mass is at D2 with in_state==2, and in_action==2 (a2->S2 common) holds 99.1% of the mass. a1->S2 rare has 849 active steps (0.9% of mass, precision 0.007). It never fires before ep_trial 50. Precision by ep_trial bin: 50-58 0.016, 58-62 0.11, 62-66 0.42, 66-70 0.62, 70-80 0.81, 80-90 0.89, 90-93 0.67, 93-95 0.34, 95-97 0.07, so the 62-95 window matches the ramp.

The false positives (precision 0.72) come from graded magnitude, not from a missing condition. Inside the predicate, prev_reward==0 steps have precision 0.46 but hold only 12.5% of the mass. prev_reward==1 steps have precision 0.87. A switch after a rewarded a1 trial (prev_reward==1 & prev_action==1) has precision 0.16 but covers only about 1.4k steps. The explanation already mentions the prev_reward skew.

No binary refinement clearly beats the original on test (F1 0.813). Excluding prev rewarded a1 trials gives 0.821, excluding prev rare-unrewarded trials gives 0.821, narrowing the window to 64-93 gives 0.821, and adding choice<-1 gives 0.819. Adding prev_reward==1 lowers dev F1 to 0.793. The remaining gap is magnitude noise, so it does not justify a new predicate.
Test misses hold only 1.8% of the activation mass and are low-activation steps (about 0.02-0.23), mostly just outside the time window or in a few rare-to-S2 cases. I found no systematic missed class.

Minor: the label does not mention that firing is stronger after a rewarded previous trial and somewhat stronger when S2 is actually the good state (good==2 holds 72% of the mass, but inside the predicate precision is 0.71 for good==2 vs 0.64 for good==1). This is modulation, not a separate class. No future variables are used.
